questions.history: The failing method precedes the passing method in the same class.
questions.prediction: Issue #4464 reports successful directories persisting after a failure. Expect one failure and one success on both revisions. On the merge only the failed method’s directory and marker should remain.
questions.basis: Each method owns its own path and cleanup mode. The execution summary independently identifies which owner succeeded.
questions.refutation: The passing path survives or the failed owner loses its marker on the merge.

questions.history: Run a fresh class containing only a passing method with an ON_SUCCESS temp directory.
questions.prediction: Both revisions should report a success and remove its recorded path after execution.
questions.basis: No failure exists in the test or its children. The cleanup condition is satisfied.
questions.refutation: The recorded path still exists after the engine finishes on either revision.

questions.history: Keep method outcomes, markers and annotations fixed, but reverse the order in a second fresh run. Group final paths by which method owned them.
questions.prediction: On the merge the failed owner alone must retain its directory in both orders. Compare ownership and marker contents rather than generated directory names.
questions.basis: An independently successful owner’s cleanup policy does not depend on whether a sibling has already failed. Files.exists is an observation outside the test engine.
questions.refutation: Only reordering the methods changes which owner’s directory remains, or the wrong marker survives.
